# dsh-pet-desktop-linux
**English** | 中文

A desktop pet for DSH (DeepSeek Harness) on Linux: a small transparent,
always-on-top GTK3 window th

at floats over your desktop and animates according to
what your DSH sessions are doing — idle, worki

ng, waiting for an answer, failed,
or finished and awaiting review. It is not click-through: the win

dow keeps its
input region, so clicks on the pet land on the pet.

**Platform: Linux with X11 or XWayland only.** Windows, macOS and native Wayland
(no XWayland) are n
ot supported. See Requirements.

The window has no background and no border — the wallpaper shows through, and the
pet stays on top o
f ordinary windows. The sprite follows your DSH sessions:

> **Canonical copy:** this plugin is only published as
> `dsh-pet-desktop-linux` (no scope) under th

e `Wlaeg` account. Any other
> package with this name is not ours.
## This is not a meta-package

This plugin ships **its own working program**; it is not a bundle that only
re-exports somebody else

*its own working program**; it is not a bundle that only
re-exports somebody else's dependency list:
| Part | File | What it does |
| Desktop program | `desktop/pet.py` | The pet window itself: GTK3 transparent window, spritesheet a

nimation, right-click menu, work-status dialog |
| Host half | `lib/index.js` | Probes system depend
encies, spawns/stops the Python program, exposes the HTTP routes, reads and writes the config file |
| Browser half | `client.js` | The **Desktop Pet** panel in DSH Settings, with the packaged `locale
/{en,zh}.json` manifest strings |

The single dependency, `@michengai/dsh-codex-pet`, is used **only to read the pet
sprite sheets**. T

his plugin deliberately does not copy that artwork into its own
repository: store rules require a bu

ndle's dependencies to resolve to the original
author's published package, so this plugin depends on

the upstream npm package
and resolves the artwork path at runtime
(`require.resolve('@michengai/dsh

-codex-pet/package.json')`). See
Artwork and licensing.

The upstream plugin draws a pet **inside the DSH web page**. This plugin draws a
**separate always-o

n-top desktop window** that works while the page is in the
background, minimized, or closed. They ar
e different things, not duplicates.
## Requirements
| Item | Requirement |
| Platform | **Linux with X11 or XWayland.** Verified on Manjaro GNOME (Wayland session, pet runs th

rough XWayland) |
| DSH | Any DSH build with the Cordis plugin system that provides `webServer` and

the `settings.section` slot |
| Node | **>= 22** (DSH's own requirement) |
| Desktop session | A GTK
3-capable session. Under GNOME/Wayland the pet is an XWayland client — a **pure Wayland session with

XWayland disabled will not work** |
| npm dependencies | `@michengai/dsh-codex-pet` (artwork lookup

d disabled will not work** |

## Features
**Window**

- Borderless, transparent GTK3 window — only the pet is visible, the window
background is fully tran

sparent
- Always on top (`_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE`), so it stays above normal windows
- Sticky across wo

rkspaces (`_NET_WM_STATE_STICKY`, via `xdotool`) — no API for
this exists in GTK3, and GTK rewrites

the hints shortly after the window is
mapped, so the plugin re-applies them and self-heals if they g

et dropped
- Draggable; the position is persisted as normalized 0–1 coordinates
- Size is adjustable

(64–224 px) from the right-click menu and in the Settings panel
- Click-through is **not** implemen

ted: the window keeps its input region, so
clicks on the pet land in the pet (they are not passed to
the window behind it)
**Animation**

- The pet is drawn by cropping 192×208 cells out of the upstream spritesheet and
scaling them with `

InterpType.NEAREST`, which keeps the pixel-art edges sharp
- Each work state has its own animation r

ow, with per-frame durations (idle,
working right/left, waving, jumping, failed, waiting, running, r

eview)
- The pet looks toward the cursor (16 directions) when it comes near, but only
within a 420px

radius; beyond that it faces front again. Without the limit it
tracks every corner of the screen an

d feels like it is locked onto you. On a
multi-monitor setup it only follows within the pet's own mo

nitor — otherwise a
pet on screen A would turn toward screen B, which is nonsense
- Long session tit

les are shortened up front: measured in columns (CJK counts as
two), keeping both head and tail with

`…` in between; the full title is on the
tooltip

**Session bubble** — a pixel-art bubble beside the pet that lists every busy DSH
session, one row ea

ession bubble** — a pixel-art bubble beside the pet that lists every busy DSH
session, one row each:

- Every row reads `state · session title · age`, e.g.
`working · add gaze tracking and a bubble · 3

minutes ago`. The task name is
shown by default rather than collapsed into a bare count
- Sorted by

priority (waiting → running → failed → review), up to 8 rows; only
when more remain does it append `

…and N more sessions`
- Titles adapt to the available width (capped at 560px); the state and the age

re sessions`
